description: The sessions sidebar: the left pane of Baude's main window, 250px wide at least. From top to bottom: New session with its host picker, Open folder, search with the ⋮ menu, a host banner, the list of sessions in groups, and an Update bar at the foot. Click a session to switch to it, folder and all.
opens: key Ctrl+B or F9 (toggles the sidebar)
the Sessions sidebar button in the header bar (tooltip "Sessions sidebar (Ctrl+B)")

phone.does: The session list is the phone's home screen; opening a session replaces it, back returns to it
phone.why: One column at a time on a phone

parts.name: New session button

decisions.said: Clicking New Session should put the caret in the message box, ready to type
decisions.rule: Every app puts the focus in the new chat's message box when New session opens it

parts.shows: A flat button with a new-document icon and the words "New session", filling the row, left of the host picker. Tooltip "Ctrl+N".

actions.does: Opens a new, blank chat at once, with the focus in its message box, on the host picked beside it, in the group chosen by the rule below (switching away from the open chat first), with the header's model, effort and mode pickers to set before it's written in (see EmptyChat). This machine: in the window's folder. Another host: in the folder last used there, else that host's home. The chat is a draft on its host: it isn't listed or kept till something is sent in it, and one left empty leaves nothing behind. If that host is gone, deactivated or not known, nothing starts and a toast says why (its banner text).
Same as the button.

parts.name: New session's group rule
parts.shows: Not drawn; decides which group a new chat joins. If exactly one group is ticked in ⋮ → Groups, that one. Else, if the chats listed all belong to one group, that one. Else, if no groups are ticked-out (all listed), none. Else the open chat's group if it's ticked, else none. After starting, that group is ticked in ⋮ too if it wasn't, so the new chat is listed.

decisions.said: With only one group visible, a new session should go into that group (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: In every app a new chat joins the group the sidebar shows: the one group ticked, else the one group the listed chats are in on that host, so it stays listed

parts.name: Host picker (beside New session)
parts.shows: A flat dropdown right of New session, naming the host a new session is made on and whose chats the list shows. Its button shows the name cut with … in the middle (about 12 characters); the popup list shows every name whole, each with its name as tooltip. Choices: "local" (this machine; on the phone, its own host) first, then every other known host sorted by name, case-insensitively. A host that is gone is dimmed in the list. When only this machine exists the dropdown is dimmed and has nothing else to pick. The choice is remembered across restarts, with its name, even while the host is gone or unknown (then it's still listed, by the name it had). Tooltip "The host a new session is made on, and whose chats are listed. Right-click (or press and hold) for Add Host…".

actions.does: Opens the list of hosts (and the network is looked at again, so a host started a moment ago is offered). Picking one saves it, shows or hides the host banner for it, and re-lists the sessions of that host only.
Opens the host menu (Deactivate/Activate, Add Host…): see HostMenu.menu.json. Not when its list is open.
Touch's right-click: the same host menu, its list not opened.

decisions.said: On mobile, in the host dropdown, your phone should be `local` as it is on desktop... Not sure why it is different on mobile.
decisions.rule: Every app names the machine it runs on "local" in the host picker, first in the list (the phone's own host too); the mesh knows it by its name

parts.name: Open folder button
parts.shows: A flat button under New session with a folder-open icon and the words "Open folder…". Tooltip "Start a session in another folder".

actions.does: With this machine picked beside New session: a folder chooser opens; the folder picked gets a new, blank chat here. With another host picked: a dialog "Open a folder on <host>" over the window, with a path field (starting as the folder last used on that host, else its home; ~ means its home) and under it a list, 240 tall, of the host's folders as the field is typed (read from the host with list_dir): .. (the folder above) first, then the folders in the folder typed, else those of its parent whose names begin with the path's last part (hidden ones only once that part begins with a dot), by name; clicking one puts its path in the field and lists its folders. Cancel and Open (suggested; Enter too): Open opens a new, blank chat on that host in that folder at once, as New session does, and keeps the folder as the host's last. If that host is gone, deactivated or not known, nothing opens and a toast says why (its banner text).

phone.does: Always the "Open a folder on <host>" step, for whichever host is picked; tapping a folder in its list is clicking it
phone.why: The phone's chats are all on hosts; it has no folder chooser of its own

parts.name: Search field
parts.shows: A search entry under a small gap, placeholder "Search sessions", filling the row left of the ⋮ button.

actions.does: Filters as it changes. A session stays if the text (case-insensitive) is in its title, its folder's name as the group label shows it, its worktree's folder name, or its Bot's name; for a session on another host also its folder path and its host's name. Searching shows every match in every group at once: collapsed groups open, "Show N more" limits are lifted, the open unsaved chat is not added. Clearing restores the grouping.

parts.name: ⋮ button
parts.shows: A flat icon button (three vertical dots) right of search. Tooltip "Group by, and which groups are listed".

actions.does: Opens the Group by / Groups menu: see GroupByMenu.menu.json. Opening it, or the window coming to the front, looks at the network again for a host started a moment ago.

parts.name: Host banner
parts.shows: Between the search row and the list: an inset, outlined box with centred, wrapped text, slid down when a host is in the way. Over the chats of the host picked, which stay listed below as they were last seen. Nothing for this machine unless the network is still being looked at.

actions.does: Informational only; it hides when the host is back, activated, or another host is picked.

parts.name: Session list
parts.shows: A scrolling list (no horizontal scroll) of group headers, each followed by its session rows and, when cut short, a "Show N more" row. Scroll position and focus are kept when it is rebuilt. The open session's row is highlighted (selected). Order: Bots first (no header), then the Desktop group's chats, then groups; by folder the folder of the open chat first then by latest activity; by Created or Updated newest day first; then the Archived group at the end.

parts.name: Group header (folder)
parts.shows: A small faint label with the folder's last path part (the whole path is its tooltip; the label is cut with … in the middle). The folder of the open chat is drawn in the accent colour. Right of the name an arrow button (pointing down when open, right when collapsed; tooltips "Collapse" / "Expand"), and at the far end a + button. Special folder groups: "Unknown folder" for sessions with no folder; "No folder (Claude Desktop)" for Claude Desktop's per-chat scratch folders (all in one group). A session that ran in a git worktree is listed under its repository's folder (and its tooltip names the worktree). A folder on another host is its own group labelled "<folder> on <host>" (folder written as on that host, home as ~).

phone.does: The arrow and + are always shown

actions.does: Folds or unfolds the group; remembered across restarts. Only the Archived group starts folded. Not applied while searching.

Opens a new, blank chat in that folder at once, as New session does (tooltip "New session in <folder>"). Only if the folder exists here. For a folder on another host: the blank chat is on that host, in that folder, which becomes the folder last used there (tooltip "New session in <folder>, on <host>"), shown only while that host is alive.

parts.name: Group header (Desktop)
parts.shows: "Desktop": Claude Desktop's chats, apart from every other chat and first after the Bots, whether the list is grouped by folder, Created or Updated. Its chats are those Claude Desktop lists on the host picked (this machine's own, read from Desktop's list; another host's, as that host lists them), nested as Desktop nests them, by latest activity. Same arrow and Show N more as a folder's (8 shown); no + button.

decisions.said: Claude Desktop's chats go into a Desktop group automatically, kept apart from the rest, and are shared over the mesh so other hosts can see them and carry them on
decisions.rule: Every app puts each Claude Desktop chat in the Desktop group (unless it's been moved to another) and lists that group apart and first after the Bots, on every host. A host lists its machine's Desktop chats to the mesh with its sessions (desktop: true; taken_up: false till one is written in), so every app on every host sees them and reads them as any chat. Writing in one from another host or the phone takes it up on its host (claude --resume there). While Claude Desktop is writing one (elsewhere), every app shows it read-only, with no text box, as Baude's own Desktop chats are.

parts.name: Group header (date)
parts.shows: When grouped by Created or Updated: "Today", "Yesterday", then each of the 5 days before as "Oct 20" style (month abbreviation, day), then "Older". Same arrow; no + button. Updated: a session and its forks go together by the latest activity of any of them; a fork used today brings its parent into today. Created: a session and its forks go together by the day the session was made, the newest made first. Days regroup at local midnight, and when the window comes to the front after one.

parts.name: Show more row
parts.shows: A dimmed row "Show N more" at the end of a group cut short. Limits count top-level sessions, their forks come with them: this folder's group none; another folder 8; by day, today none, yesterday 10, an earlier day 5.

phone.does: nothing: every group lists all its sessions
phone.why: Early truncation of chats on the phone

actions.does: Shows the rest of that group (until the day changes for date groups).

parts.name: Session row

phone.does: At least 48dp tall (40 of the phone's units at Global Scale 1.0, Theme.kt's Gap.homeRow), the title and dot centred in it
phone.why: Android's least touch target: rows the desktop's height are too small to tap

parts.shows: One line: the title (for a Bot whose host is gone, its name, never its chat's title; a title too long fades out at the cut, no …), then a status dot at the far right. The title is "(untitled)" if it has none. A session on another host that is gone shows its title (a Bot: its name) dimmed with a crossed-out cloud icon (schema/icons/baude/baude-no-connection-symbolic.svg) before the dot, tooltip "No connection" (not for a deactivated host: just dimmed). A chat its host holds messages for shows a small "held" tag before the dot. A chat open that is already listed (archived, say) is listed only there, highlighted. A chat open but not yet written in shows as "New session" at the top of its folder (never while blank), and has no right-click menu. Tooltip (several lines, those that apply): title (a Bot: its name); its folder; "N message(s) held for it, to send or delete in it"; "On <host> (<address>)" with ", deactivated" or ", gone from the network since <time ago>"; "Group <name>"; "Worktree <name> of <folder>"; the source line (for a session of this machine's Claude Desktop or Claude Code, and "<host>, on the network" for a session on a host); "N earlier copy/copies of this conversation hidden".
text: {n} message(s) held for it, to send or delete in it
{n} earlier copy/copies of this conversation hidden

actions.does: Switches to that session: its history is drawn, its folder becomes the window's folder. A session on a host has its transcript fetched first. The open session: nothing. Clicking in the Feedback tab or a code page returns to the chat.
The session menu: see SessionRowMenu.menu.json.
Rename… the focused (or selected) session. Not for the unsaved open chat, or a session whose host is gone.

parts.name: Fork nesting
parts.shows: A fork sits under the session it came from, indented 18px per level, joined by a thin tree line: down from the foot of the parent's row (for a Bot, 1px under its picture, 5px in from its left edge) to its last child, then a corner across to that child. A fork named "<parent's title> (…)" shows only the "…" part, in a distinct fork style. A Claude Desktop side session or fork sits under the chat Claude Desktop says it came from, in that chat's group whatever its own folder. A chat a Bot started is under that agent. A chat an agent on another host started (its spawned_by a chat of another host, none of its own host's: an archived or gone-host chat counts, one whose agent is deleted doesn't), and any chat that one started in turn on its host, is listed only under that agent, never among its own host's chats: under it whichever host's chats are listed, if the agent is listed (not deleted here, or missed by a search), and nowhere otherwise. An archived agent's chats are under it in Archived, whatever host they're on. The phone's home list and This phone's agents follow the same rule. Forks are found within a folder, by date too.

decisions.said: On phone, the rule where subagents started on another machine by a Bot are not visible... Is not followed.... Please make sure that rule is followed.
decisions.rule: Every app lists a chat a Bot on another host started (and any chat that one started in turn) only under that Bot, never among its own host's chats, and nowhere when the Bot isn't listed

decisions.said: On the phone, the bars from a Bot to its subagent chats don't start near its icon; do as the desktop does (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app starts the tree line from a Bot to the chats under it just under the Bot's picture (1px under it, 5px in from its left edge)

parts.name: Desktop chats
parts.shows: Chats of Claude Desktop (and Claude Code) listed with this machine's own, by their last-used time as Claude Desktop reckons it (unless typed in since elsewhere). Several stale copies of one conversation are folded into one row (the tooltip says how many). Desktop-archived chats show in Archived unless unarchived here.

parts.name: Active elsewhere
parts.shows: A session not open here but being run by another program (Claude Desktop, a terminal) or left mid-turn with its claude running in the background shows the working dot (grey, pulsing), or yellow if it asks something, while that goes on, then blue for a minute after, as file changes are watched with no polling. Opening it shows it read-only/live-tailing: see the chat's banner (not this area).

decisions.said: Switching chats while the Ongoing Feedback tab is shown left it on the Feedback tab instead of opening the chat
decisions.rule: In every app, clicking a chat in the list while another main tab (Feedback, a file's code) is shown switches to the chat's tab and opens that chat.

decisions.said:
Increase row height of:

* Trainscripts on the home page
decisions.rule: Every app draws its chat list's rows tall enough to tap where it's touched: on a touch screen a chat row is at least 48dp (the least touch target) with its title and dot centred, and a Bot row twice a chat's

decisions.said: <dead> is shown when a connection ides. This is not needed, you should just use a cloud icon with a slash going through it (no connection) to indicate this on mobile and dsesktop.
decisions.rule: Every app marks a chat whose host is gone with the crossed-out cloud (schema/icons/baude/baude-no-connection-symbolic.svg, tooltip "No connection") and never with a "dead" word

parts.name: Bot row
parts.shows: For a session on a host that is a Bot (top level only, its host reachable; a Bot whose host is gone is a session row showing its name, dimmed, with the crossed-out cloud): twice a chat's height: a round avatar with the Bot's picture (its initials until it has one), set into the page: see README's A picture is set into the page, the Bot's name in bold on one line, a "held" tag if any, the status dot. The tree line to the chats under it starts under its picture (see Fork nesting). A Bot has only its Name: the row never shows its chat's title or any second line. Bots are listed first in the list with no header, the last used first, each with what is under it (its forks and threads, whatever host). By date, Bots are among the chats by time. Tooltip: name; folder; "On <host> (<address>)"; held; "Group <name>"; worktree (never the chat's title).

actions.does: As a session row.
The session menu, with Bot Settings…: see SessionRowMenu.menu.json.

parts.name: Archived group
parts.shows: At the end of the list a group headed "Archived" (no + button), folded at first, holding archived sessions (archived here, in Claude Desktop, or on their host) with their forks. Rows look as normal; their menu says Unarchive instead of Archive.

parts.name: Changed by Meta
parts.shows: A chat that Meta (the assistant) changed and that isn't kept yet is marked in its row, with Keep and Undo; one Meta deleted stays listed, struck through, until kept; a deleted one (ghost) has no menu and doesn't open. Belongs with Meta's own entry.

parts.name: Update bar
parts.shows: At the very foot, under a rule from the list, only while a new version waits to be restarted onto: a flat button "Update" at the left. Tooltip: "Waiting for:" with bullet lines of what the restart waits for, or "A new version is ready".

phone.does: The phone's own updater: the Update bar at the foot of home (Update.kt)
phone.why: The phone installs builds, not a git checkout

actions.does: Restarts onto the new version now (asking first if that would stop something running).

decisions.said: Asked for the Update Available button to be white and not bold.
decisions.rule: Every app's Update button is in the text's own colour (white on a dark bar), not bold, not the accent.

parts.name: Sidebar toggle
parts.shows: The whole sidebar slides away and back as one pane on the left; the header bar's sidebar button toggles it too.

phone.why: The session list is the phone's home screen; keyboard shortcuts only

actions.does: Shows or hides the sidebar (also F9). Handled before the focused text box so it works inside text fields.
Same.

parts.name: Status dot
parts.shows: A small round dot at the right of each row (also in Bot rows), same size as the icon size set in Settings → Size. Working: grey (the text colour at 55% strength) and pulsing, tooltip "Working". Waiting: yellow (#e5a50a), tooltip "Waiting for your answer" (a question or permission prompt needs an answer). Done: blue (#3584e4), tooltip "Finished — waiting for input" (the turn finished, waiting for your next message). Inactive: not drawn at all. The open session's dot follows the live chat. For other sessions on this machine: working while another program is mid-turn in the file, waiting if it asks, done for a minute after its last write, else inactive; mid-turn but silent 10 minutes counts as inactive. For a session on a host: as that host last said (working, waiting, else inactive; inactive while the host is gone).

states.name: empty list
states.shows: Nothing is drawn: no rows and no headers (a search with no match, or no sessions on the picked host or in the picked groups, leaves a blank list). Only the open chat once it has something typed in appears.

states.name: loading
states.shows: The first read of a slow list shows the newest sessions as they are found, then the whole list when done; the list refreshes in the background, unchanged files from a cache.

states.name: host gone
states.shows: Host banner "Can't connect to <host> at the moment", or "…at the moment: <why>" if the last try said why; the host's chats listed dimmed with the crossed-out cloud icon; their menu offers only Delete. The host is also dimmed in the host picker.

states.name: host deactivated
states.shows: Host banner "<host> is deactivated"; its chats dimmed, no crossed-out cloud; New session toasts that text.

states.name: host unknown
states.shows: A host picked that the network doesn't have now (forgotten, or a mesh member not listed yet): listed in the picker by the name it had; banner "Looking for <host> on the network…"; its chats absent.

states.name: host stopping or restarting
states.shows: Banner "<host> stopping…" / "<host> restarting…", with a count when known ("<host> stopping — N of M processes to stop", "… every process stopped"); this machine's host process is called "Daemon".

states.name: grouped by folder
states.shows: Default. The open chat's folder first, others by latest activity.

states.name: grouped by Created or Updated
states.shows: Today, Yesterday, the last five days, Older: by the day each chat was made, or last used.

states.name: searching
states.shows: Groups all open, every match shown, no Show more rows.

states.name: groups filtered
states.shows: Only the sessions of the groups checked in ⋮ → Groups (see GroupByMenu.menu.json); checking Groups lists every one again.

removed.name: New session form (a dialog of host, folder, group, prompt, model, effort and mode: the desktop's from a folder's + on another host, or on this machine while a new chat here wouldn't be listed; the phone's from a folder's + and Open folder…)
removed.why: A new chat is only made on its host once something's sent in it, so New session, a folder's + and Open folder… (after its folder step) open a blank chat at once; its model, effort and mode are the header's pickers

removed.name: Session tags (on network sessions: set in the start dialog, shown on sidebar rows, searched)
removed.why: The owner called network session tags a useless feature and asked for them to be dropped (paraphrased); groups stay.

removed.name: Folder name at the right of a chat's sidebar row (grouped by day)
removed.why: The owner: it's nearly always truncated and the chat name says what's needed, so drop it (paraphrased).

removed.name: worktree pill on a chat row
removed.why: The owner doesn't care for pills naming a chat's worktree: if the agent is in a worktree it says so. The tooltip still names the worktree and search still finds it.

decisions.said: an archived chat that is open shows under Today, and twice in the left bar
decisions.rule: A chat that is open and already listed (archived included) is listed once, only where it already is, highlighted; it is never added again as a new unsaved chat.
